title_en: Chinese History (5/20): Zhang Qian and the Silk Road
note_en: To say how long something lasted, Chinese puts the duration right after the verb (often after 了), with no word like "for": 被扣留了整整十年 "was held for a full ten years." English needs "for" and can move the time phrase around, but in Chinese verb + duration is fixed; putting 十年 before the verb (十年被扣留) would be wrong. 整整 "a whole, a full" adds weight to the length.
